dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.pnlInfo:
P&L (Profit and Loss) — how much you have won or lost.

Example: €10 stake at 2.0 odds, win → P&L = +€10
dashboard.roiInfo:
ROI (Return on Investment) — return on investment in %.

Formula: P&L / Total staked × 100%

Example: won €5 from €20 staked → ROI = 25%
dashboard.tapDayHint: Tap a day to see turnover, won, lost and profit
dashboard.tipBody: Turnover at the top follows the period (7d / 30d / all). Tap a day on the chart to see turnover, won, lost and profit. "Expand" opens the full day-by-day table with filters.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.proMsg: Full analytics (7 breakdowns) is available in SharkLog Pro
analytics.subtitle: Where you stand — short and complete
analytics.proFeatureFull: Full analytics: streaks, records, CLV, bet timing
analytics.biggestWinInfo:
Your best bet in the selected period: the largest net win on a single bet (payout minus stake).

Under the value — the event it came from.
analytics.biggestLossInfo:
Your worst bet in the selected period: the largest net loss on a single bet.

Lost free bets are not counted — their P&L is 0; it was not your money.
analytics.edgeInfo:
Compares your win rate (WR) with the break-even rate at your average odds.

Break-even (b/e) = 100 / average odds. Example: average odds 2.20 → you need to win 45.5% of bets to break even. If your WR is higher, you have an edge and come out ahead over time.

This is an estimate; it becomes reliable from about 100 settled bets.
analytics.drawdownInfo:
The deepest fall of cumulative P&L from a peak to a trough over your betting history.

This is the main measure of risk: it shows the worst drop in money you have lived through. "−88% from peak" means that at the worst moment you had lost 88% of the profit you had built up.

The smaller the drawdown at the same ROI, the steadier the strategy and the lower the risk of blowing the bank.
analytics.smallSampleEdge: Small sample ({{n}}/{{min}}) — the edge and % are not stable yet
analytics.luckNeutral: The result is within normal variance — this sample cannot tell decisions apart from luck.
analytics.luckAbove: The result is above what the odds alone would give. Part of that is luck, and luck does not repeat on demand.
analytics.luckBelow: The result is below what the odds alone would give. A run like this is a normal part of the long game, not a reason to change everything.
analytics.sigmaInfo:
The baseline is break-even: odds of 2.50 mean a 40% chance, and if you hit at exactly that rate you end at zero.

So the question is not "how much did I make" but "how far did the result move from zero compared with how far it COULD move by chance". That ratio is σ (sigma).

Up to 1σ is normal variance. Beyond 2σ the result is unlikely to be luck alone: you are most likely really finding value (or are systematically wrong).

The estimate is strict with you: the bookmaker's margin is built into the odds, so the real zero sits slightly below break-even. Being positive on this scale already means beating the margin.
analytics.spreadInfo:
How far the result could swing on its own, with no skill at all — just because bets either land or they do not.

It is calculated from your real stakes and odds: the bigger the stakes and the higher the odds, the wider the swing. If your profit or loss is smaller than this figure, it proves nothing.
analytics.smallSampleLuck: Small sample ({{n}}/{{min}}) — over a short run almost any result fits within variance
analytics.clvEmpty: Add the "closing odds" when you log a bet, and the key professional metric will appear here: how much better your odds are than the line before kick-off.
analytics.clvAvgInfo:
Closing Line Value — how much better your odds are, on average, than the closing line.

CLV = (your odds / closing odds − 1) × 100%. Example: you took 2.10, the line closed at 2.00 → CLV +5%.

A consistently positive CLV is the main sign that you are beating the line rather than just getting lucky. Fill in the "closing odds" when you log a bet.
analytics.beatLineInfo:
The share of bets where your odds ended up higher than the closing odds.

Consistently above 50% means you get a better price than the market: you find value before the line moves.

bankroll.title: Bankroll
bankroll.kellyInfo:
Kelly Criterion helps calculate the optimal bet size.

Formula: f = (p × b − q) / b
where p = win probability, q = 1 − p, b = odds − 1

Example: 55% probability, 2.0 odds, €100 bankroll
f = (0.55 × 1 − 0.45) / 1 = 10% → stake €10
bankroll.proMsg: Bankroll tracker and Kelly calculator are available in subscription
bankroll.chartEmpty: Not enough data for a chart
bankroll.kellyHelp:
A formula for the optimal stake size, based on your estimate of the probability and the odds.

Example: odds 2.10, your probability estimate 55% → Half-Kelly ≈ 2.4% of the bank.

We recommend Half-Kelly (50% of full Kelly) — it reduces variance.

desc.starter: Low risk and small stakes to build experience. Focus on discipline and tracking your stats.
desc.professional: Deep involvement, detailed analysis and strict bankroll management. Bet only on well-researched events.
desc.conservative: Capital protection first. Bet on heavy favourites with high probability at small stake sizes.
desc.aggressive: High odds and fast bankroll growth potential. Requires nerves of steel and strict discipline.
desc.value: Find bets where the real probability exceeds the bookmaker's estimate. Moderate risk, long-term profit.
desc.balanced: Optimal balance of risk and return. Diverse bets with solid bankroll management.

risk.conservative: A conservative approach protects the bankroll from large drawdowns — preserving capital is the priority.
risk.aggressive: High risk tolerance opens the door to higher odds and faster bankroll growth — but demands iron discipline.
risk.moderate: Moderate risk is the optimal balance: the bankroll grows without the threat of critical drawdowns.

exp.beginner: At the start, the most important thing is to collect 100+ bets for reliable stats — profit comes with experience.
exp.professional: Professional-level experience lets you work with line movement, live betting and value hunting.
exp.experienced: Accumulated experience lets you separate value bets from noise and build strategy on data, not intuition.

time.minimal: With limited time, bet only on well-covered matches — don't guess on poorly-researched events.
time.intensive: High involvement gives a competitive edge: tracking line movement and live betting opportunities.

risk.conservative: Bet only when 75%+ confident — skipping an event is not a loss, it's discipline
risk.moderate: Don't adjust stake size based on "confidence" — discipline beats intuition
risk.aggressive: Hard stop-loss: a 25% drawdown in one week means a minimum 3-day break

exp.beginner: First 3 months: data collection only. Don't expect profit — the goal is stats for analysis
exp.professional: Track line movement: a sharp odds shift 1–2 hours before a match signals insider information
exp.experienced: Keep detailed stats per bet type — cut non-performing markets once a month

sport.football: Study last 5 matches and H2H — home/away form is especially important in football
sport.esports: Watch active rosters: player substitutions 24h before a match sharply change the odds
sport.tennis: Factor in court surface and physical load from recent tournaments — tennis is physically demanding
sport.hockey: The goaltender decides up to 40% of hockey outcomes — always check who's in net before betting
sport.mixed: Specialise in at most 2–3 sports — spreading across 5+ halves your ROI

focus.topMatches: With limited time, bet only on top matches: more media coverage = fewer mispriced events
focus.liveLines: Use live line monitoring — a sharp odds shift 1–2 hours pre-match often contains value
focus.roiTarget: Target ROI: a steady 5–8% per month yields 60–100% bankroll growth per year
focus.lossLimit: Set a personal monthly loss limit and never break it under any circumstances

odds.low: Favourites at 1.30–1.70 win 65–80% of the time. The key is stake sizing and discipline, not chasing high odds.
odds.high: High odds (2.50+) imply a win probability of 40% or less. Profit requires a large sample (200+ bets) and strict selection.
odds.mid: The 1.70–2.50 range is optimal: sufficient win probability (40–60%) with acceptable returns. Most value sits here.

betTypeRationale.football: Totals (over/under) and handicaps in football carry more value than 1X2 — bookmakers price winners well but misjudge scores.
betTypeRationale.hockey: Hockey totals ±0.5 and handicaps -1.5/+1.5 are often mispriced — fertile ground for value.
betTypeRationale.tennis: Game handicaps offer the best edge in tennis. Set totals suit those tracking physical condition.
betTypeRationale.esports: Map and round handicaps are the main value market in esports. Outright results are too popular with casual bettors.
betTypeRationale.mixed: When covering multiple sports, focus on outrights and totals — they are easiest to analyse consistently.
betTypeRationale.default: Choose markets where you have a competitive edge over the bookmaker.
